items.author: sametulutea
items.context: @sametulutea (25.708 seguidores, en inglés): terminó su DCA en BTC entre $75k y $60k y dice que sus métricas de riesgo (costo base de holders de corto plazo, MVRV, Z-score, SOPR) muestran BTC bastante sobrevendido; su costo base del ciclo ronda $67k. Cuenta mediana con un post que despega (35 likes, 4 bookmarks y 2.842 impresiones en ~1h20) y solo 3 respuestas; menciona MVRV, calza con temperatura de mercado.
items.suggested_text:
Stacking those four makes sense because each one measures something different: STH cost basis shows where recent buyers are underwater, MVRV and its Z-score compare price with the market's aggregate on-chain cost, and SOPR tells you whether coins are actually being spent at a loss. When all of them lean the same way, it's usually capitulation, not noise.

I track a similar composite (MVRV, price vs. the 200-week average, drawdown from the ATH and volatility-adjusted 90-day momentum, 25% each), and it went from 99.29 to 0.67 in 364 days. A reading like that says the market is cold; it doesn't say when it turns.

That's the nuance with "oversold": it describes the state of holders, not the calendar. In 2018 and 2022 MVRV spent months near or below 1 while price chopped sideways, which is why the cost basis you build in that zone tends to matter more than nailing the exact low.
